person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: extracellular vesicles, and - unusually - THE TERMS THE FIELD USES TO NAME THEM, which this document treats as an object to be governed rather than as background
span.quote: Definition: The term ‘extracellular vesicles’ (EVs) refers to particles that are released from cells, are delimited by a lipid bilayer, and cannot replicate on their own (i.e., do not contain a functional nucleus).

span.label: which of the field's terms can be defended by what a measurement can actually show, and what minimal information a study must report
span.quote: In general, ISEV recommends use of the generic term ‘EV’ and operational extensions of this term instead of inconsistently defined and sometimes misleading terms such as ‘exosomes’ and ‘ectosomes’ that are associated with biogenesis pathways that are difficult to establish.

span.label: a society-wide reporting standard whose central move is to REPLACE biogenesis-based names with operational ones - names that state what was measured rather than how the particle is presumed to have been made
span.quote: In general, ISEV recommends use of the generic term ‘EV’ and operational extensions of this term instead of inconsistently defined and sometimes misleading terms such as ‘exosomes’ and ‘ectosomes’ that are associated with biogenesis pathways that are difficult to establish.

span.label: method
span.quote: By contrast, MISEV IS NOT: A one‐size‐fits‐all blueprint, a comprehensive checklist of ‘dos and don'ts’, or a substitute for careful expert judgement. There is no technique or platform that is absolutely required or prohibited by MISEV.

span.label: particles released from cells, delimited by a lipid bilayer, that cannot replicate on their own - and that no available separation method isolates by the property their popular names refer to
span.quote: Definition: The term ‘extracellular vesicles’ (EVs) refers to particles that are released from cells, are delimited by a lipid bilayer, and cannot replicate on their own (i.e., do not contain a functional nucleus).

span.label: an updated consensus document from the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles, each section carrying a recorded vote of roughly 1,000 survey respondents
span.term: an updated consensus document from the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles, each section carrying a recorded vote of roughly 1,000 survey respondents
span.quote: Consensus: 89.3% (891) of MISEV2023 survey respondents agreed “completely,” and 10.7% (107) agreed “mostly” with Section 1: An introduction to ISEV and MISEV. No respondents disagreed (“mostly” or “completely”), and no respondents stated that they had no opinion and/or expertise.

span.label: the two classical subtypes are defined by ROUTE: an exosome leaves via the multivesicular body, an ectosome buds from the cell surface. That is a biogenesis distinction, and it is the one the separation methods do not make
span.quote: The term ‘exosome’ refers to EVs from internal compartments of the cell that are released via the multivesicular body (MVB), while the term ‘ectosome’ (a.k.a., microvesicle, microparticle) refers to EVs from the cell surface.

span.label: EV and NVEP are separated in the definition by a single structural fact - whether lipids form a delimiting bilayer - and in practice the two co-isolate, with NVEPs possibly OUTNUMBERING EVs in the sample
span.quote: (NVEPs) are all non‐EV particles made from cell‐derived components of one or more molecular classes (e.g., proteins, nucleic acids); lipids, if present, do not form a delimiting bilayer membrane. NVEPs and EVs may have overlapping physicochemical properties, and NVEPs may greatly outnumber EVs in biological matrices.

span.label: A STANDARDS BODY FORMALLY DEPRECATES THE FIELD'S TWO MOST-USED TERMS: `ISEV RECOMMENDS USE OF THE GENERIC TERM ‘EV’ and operational extensions of this term INSTEAD OF INCONSISTENTLY DEFINED AND SOMETIMES MISLEADING TERMS SUCH AS ‘EXOSOMES’ AND ‘ECTOSOMES’`. In the nomenclature table both are marked `Discouraged unless subcellular origin can be demonstrated` - a CONDITIONAL deprecation, not a ban.
span.quote: In general, ISEV recommends use of the generic term ‘EV’ and operational extensions of this term instead of inconsistently defined and sometimes misleading terms such as ‘exosomes’ and ‘ectosomes’ that are associated with biogenesis pathways that are difficult to establish

span.label: AND THIS CLOSES A COMPLAINT MADE BY THE SAME BODY NINE YEARS EARLIER. `lotvall2014`, the founding document of this series, said `The term ‘exosomes’ is the most commonly used word to designate ANY TYPE OF EV ... The ACTUAL MEANING of this word, however, is NOT UNIVERSALLY ACCEPTED`. It diagnosed the problem and did nothing about the word. MISEV2023 DISCOURAGES IT. A complaint in 2014 became a deprecation in 2023, by the same society, across three staged documents.
span.quote: In general, ISEV recommends use of the generic term ‘EV’ and operational extensions of this term instead of inconsistently defined and sometimes misleading terms such as ‘exosomes’ and ‘ectosomes’ that are associated with biogenesis pathways that are difficult to establish

span.label: THE VERSION CHAIN IS NAMED IN THE ABSTRACT, WITH BOTH PREDECESSORS: `ISEV UPDATES its ‘Minimal Information for Studies of Extracellular Vesicles’, which was FIRST PUBLISHED IN 2014 AND THEN IN 2018 AS MISEV2014 AND MISEV2018, RESPECTIVELY`. The 2014 document does not contain the string `MISEV` anywhere - both the expansion and the number were assigned to it retrospectively by its successors.
span.quote: the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles (ISEV) updates its ‘Minimal Information for Studies of Extracellular Vesicles’, which was first published in 2014 and then in 2018 as MISEV2014 and MISEV2018, respectively

span.label: THE FIELD'S TWO MOST FAMOUS TERMS ARE DISCOURAGED BY ITS OWN SOCIETY, on the ground that they are `associated with biogenesis pathways that are difficult to establish` - the defining property is not one the assay reports
span.quote: In general, ISEV recommends use of the generic term ‘EV’ and operational extensions of this term instead of inconsistently defined and sometimes misleading terms such as ‘exosomes’ and ‘ectosomes’ that are associated with biogenesis pathways that are difficult to establish.

span.label: there are NO UNIVERSAL MOLECULAR MARKERS of ectosomes, exosomes or other EV subtypes, and most separation techniques do not enrich for EVs produced by different mechanisms - so the biogenesis-based subtype cannot be shown even in principle by the standard workflow
span.quote: Unfortunately, most EV separation techniques do not enrich for EVs produced by different mechanisms, and definitive characterisation of biogenesis‐based subtypes is also difficult, with no universal molecular markers of ectosomes, exosomes or other EV subtypes. Therefore, ISEV discourages the use of biogenesis‐based terms unless such an EV population is specifically separated and characterised.

span.label: THE FALLBACK TERMS FAIL THE SAME WAY ONE LEVEL DOWN: `small` and `large` have no strict consensus on their cut-offs, and the separation methods yield populations with overlapping size profiles
span.quote: However, although ‘small’ might generally refer to EVs <200 nm in diameter, there is no strict consensus on upper and lower size cut‐offs, and it has also become clear that many separation methods, such as dUC, yield EV populations with overlapping size profiles.

span.label: most EP separation methods co-isolate NVEPs with EVs and many characterisation methods do not identify EVs specifically - the boundary the definition is drawn on is not one the instrument resolves
span.quote: As a result, most EP separation methods result in NVEP/EV co‐isolation. Similarly, many EP characterisation methods do not identify EVs specifically.

span.label: each section was put to a survey of the society's membership and the agreement rate is printed with it - 89.3% completely and 10.7% mostly on Section 1, with no dissent and no abstention recorded
span.note: eliminates: a standard that presents a committee's preference as the field's consensus without ever measuring whether the field agrees · outcome: held
span.quote: Consensus: 89.3% (891) of MISEV2023 survey respondents agreed “completely,” and 10.7% (107) agreed “mostly” with Section 1: An introduction to ISEV and MISEV. No respondents disagreed (“mostly” or “completely”), and no respondents stated that they had no opinion and/or expertise.

span.label: the document states in its own words what it is NOT - not a blueprint, not a checklist, not a substitute for judgement - and that no technique or platform is required or prohibited
span.note: eliminates: a reporting standard being read as a methodological mandate, and used to block work that does not fit a reviewer's reading of it · outcome: held
span.quote: By contrast, MISEV IS NOT: A one‐size‐fits‐all blueprint, a comprehensive checklist of ‘dos and don'ts’, or a substitute for careful expert judgement. There is no technique or platform that is absolutely required or prohibited by MISEV.

span.label: the remedy offered for an unprovable claim is RENAMING rather than rejection: an `exosome` study that cannot prove biogenesis is to be presented as an EV study
span.note: eliminates: a nomenclature rule that would suppress publication of sound work whose category claim happens to be unverifiable · outcome: held
span.quote: For example, an ‘exosome’ or ‘ectosome’ study that does not prove biogenesis can be presented instead as about EVs

span.label: whether EVs can be separated from non-vesicular extracellular particles by the methods in routine use
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the document reports that most methods co-isolate them and that NVEPs may outnumber EVs in the sample · outcome: failed
span.quote: (NVEPs) are all non‐EV particles made from cell‐derived components of one or more molecular classes (e.g., proteins, nucleic acids); lipids, if present, do not form a delimiting bilayer membrane. NVEPs and EVs may have overlapping physicochemical properties, and NVEPs may greatly outnumber EVs in biological matrices.

span.label: ectosome
span.quote: The term ‘exosome’ refers to EVs from internal compartments of the cell that are released via the multivesicular body (MVB), while the term ‘ectosome’ (a.k.a., microvesicle, microparticle) refers to EVs from the cell surface.

span.label: Extracellular particles
span.quote: Extracellular particles (EPs) is the preferred overarching term for cell‐derived multimolecular assemblies in the nanometre to micron size range, including both EVs and non‐vesicular entities

span.label: naturally
span.quote: ‘naturally’ (as in ‘naturally released’) has been removed to avoid unintended exclusion of engineered EVs or EVs produced under various cell culture conditions

span.label: nomenclature
span.quote: the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles (ISEV) updates its ‘Minimal Information for Studies of Extracellular Vesicles’, which was first published in 2014 and then in 2018 as MISEV2014 and MISEV2018, respectively

span.label: extracellular vesicle - AS DEFINED HERE: released from cells, delimited by a lipid bilayer, cannot replicate on its own. Three properties, of which only the bilayer distinguishes an EV from the far more numerous non-vesicular particles it co-isolates with
span.quote: Definition: The term ‘extracellular vesicles’ (EVs) refers to particles that are released from cells, are delimited by a lipid bilayer, and cannot replicate on their own (i.e., do not contain a functional nucleus).

span.label: exosome - A BIOGENESIS TERM, AND THE DOCUMENT'S CENTRAL CASE. It names EVs released via the multivesicular body. ISEV discourages it unless the population was actually separated and characterised, because no marker identifies it and no standard method enriches for it. THE NAME ASSERTS A HISTORY THE MEASUREMENT DID NOT OBSERVE
span.quote: Unfortunately, most EV separation techniques do not enrich for EVs produced by different mechanisms, and definitive characterisation of biogenesis‐based subtypes is also difficult, with no universal molecular markers of ectosomes, exosomes or other EV subtypes. Therefore, ISEV discourages the use of biogenesis‐based terms unless such an EV population is specifically separated and characterised.

span.label: operational term - the document's remedy and its own coinage: a prefix on `EV` stating the characteristic the population was actually separated on - size, density, molecular composition, cellular origin. DEFINE BY WHAT WAS MEASURED
span.quote: Regarding ‘operational terms’ that can be added as a prefix to ‘EV’ (Table 2 ), their use continues to be encouraged with caution if one or more EV subtypes are separated on the basis of characteristics such as size, density, molecular composition or cellular origin. We urge careful and clear definition of these operational terms.

span.label: `naturally` - A WORD DELETED FROM A DEFINITION AND THE DELETION MINUTED. MISEV2018 said EVs are `naturally released`; MISEV2023 removes it so engineered EVs are not excluded by accident. A field editing its category boundary in public and saying why
span.quote: The current definition of EV is retained from MISEV2018, except that the 2018 use of the word ‘naturally’ (as in ‘naturally released’) has been removed to avoid unintended exclusion of engineered EVs or EVs produced under various cell culture conditions.

span.label: `extracellular vesicles` - THE 2023 DEFINITION, ALL THREE CLAUSES NEGATIVE OR STRUCTURAL AND NONE ABOUT ORIGIN: `particles that are RELEASED FROM CELLS, are DELIMITED BY A LIPID BILAYER, and CANNOT REPLICATE ON THEIR OWN`. Nothing about where in the cell they came from - which is the whole point of the accompanying deprecations.
span.quote: The term ‘extracellular vesicles’ (EVs) refers to particles that are released from cells, are delimited by a lipid bilayer, and cannot replicate on their own

span.label: A WORD REMOVED FROM A DEFINITION BECAUSE OF WHAT IT EXCLUDED: `‘naturally’ (as in ‘naturally released’) HAS BEEN REMOVED TO AVOID UNINTENDED EXCLUSION OF ENGINEERED EVs or EVs produced under various cell culture conditions`. The extension was wrong at one edge and a single adverb was deleted to fix it.
span.quote: ‘naturally’ (as in ‘naturally released’) has been removed to avoid unintended exclusion of engineered EVs or EVs produced under various cell culture conditions

span.label: THE VERSIONS ARE CUMULATIVE, NOT REPLACING: `The earlier MISEV recommendations REMAIN LARGELY OR ENTIRELY VALID, and MISEV2023 SHOULD BE READ IN THE CONTEXT OF THE PREVIOUS DOCUMENTS.` A reader cannot use the current version alone, which is the opposite of how CONSORT 2010 supersedes CONSORT 2001.
span.quote: The earlier MISEV recommendations remain largely or entirely valid, and MISEV2023 should be read in the context of the previous documents

span.label: `size` and `diameter` - USED INTERCHANGEABLY ACROSS INSTRUMENTS THAT DERIVE THEM DIFFERENTLY: `While ‘size’ and ‘diameter’ are often used interchangeably BETWEEN MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGIES, THE WAY IN WHICH THEY ARE DERIVED CAN ALSO RESULT IN CONSISTENT DIFFERENCES IN MEASUREMENT TECHNIQUES`. The words are traded as equivalent while the instruments behind them are not.
span.quote: While ‘size’ and ‘diameter’ are often used interchangeably between measurement methodologies, the way in which they are derived can also result in consistent differences in measurement techniques

span.label: critiques → biogenesis-based EV nomenclature - `exosome`, `ectosome`, `microvesicle` - on the ground that no universal marker identifies the subtypes and standard separation does not enrich for them

Therefore, ISEV discourages the use of biogenesis‐based terms unless such an EV population is specifically separated and characterised.
